commit_message: feat: add withRetry helper with exponential backoff
summary: New async retry helper with four vitest tests; the no-retry and backoff behaviour is not actually pinned.

defects.description: `does not retry client errors` asserts inside a catch block with no expect.assertions / fail-on-resolve, so it passes if withRetry resolves instead of throwing. It should use `await expect(...).rejects` (or expect.assertions(n)).

The same test checks `toHaveBeenCalled()` instead of `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, so retrying 4xx errors is not caught: mutating `err.status < 500` (to `<= 500`, `>= 500`, or `false`) survives. The name promises the no-retry behaviour that the body never checks.
`gives up after the configured retries` checks only that it rejects, not that fn ran retries+1 = 3 times; `attempt <= opts.retries` -> `<` survives. Off-by-one in retry count is untested.

Every test passes `noSleep` and never inspects the delays, so the backoff schedule (`delayMs * 2 ** attempt`, and `attempt < opts.retries` controlling the last sleep) is unpinned; arithmetic mutants survive. A `vi.fn()` sleep should be asserted to receive [10, 20] for retries: 2.

hand.find: if (err instanceof HttpError && err.status < 500) throw err;
hand.replace: if (err instanceof HttpError && err.status < 500) return undefined as T;
